pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Fatal Familial Insomnia (FFI) THE SMOKING GUN: Polysomnography revealing a total loss of sleep spindles and K-complexes, coupled with severe sympathetic overdrive that is completely refractory to pharmacological sleep agents. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Fatal Familial Insomnia is an extremely rare, autosomal dominant prion disease caused by a point mutation at codon 178 of the PRNP gene (D178N) linked to methionine at codon 129. The disease causes misfolded prion proteins to selectively target and destroy the mediodorsal and anterior ventral nuclei of the thalamus. Because these specific thalamic nuclei regulate sleep-wake cycles and autonomic balance, their atrophy leads to a continuous, irreversible suppression of slow-wave sleep and uninhibited sympathetic hyperactivation.
